text:
Sidney Crosby is sixth on the NHL's all-time scoring list. He passed Marcel Dionne in the win in Los Angeles on Nov. 7, which reporters put at 1,772 career points, and he did it at 39 on a Penguins team that had been losing. Only five players in league history have more.

The season line, 13 points in 18 games, undersells the player. His scoring rate of 2.22 points per 60 is below our talent range for him (about 2.5 to 3.4), and he is getting 1.08 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, more than last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking still had him in the 99th percentile of forwards as a setup man, and Evolving-Hockey said his chances last season were better than his goals.

With Evgeni Malkin on his wing lately and trade talk swirling around Pittsburgh's veterans, Crosby is the constant. Our projection lands him around 75 points; we'd lean to the high side of that.
headline: Crosby passes Dionne, and the chances are there
